Drink not the cup except with a trusted brother * one pure of origin, traced back to worthy forebears.
For wine is like the wind: if it blows over perfume * it turns sweet, and it stinks if it passes over carrion.
sentences.i:
Drink the cup with none but a brother you trust * one of clean stock, sprung from worthy forebears —
for wine is like the wind: let it cross a bed of perfume * and it turns sweet; let it cross carrion, and it reeks.
sentences.n: The simile turns on the idea that wine, like a breeze, takes on the character of whatever — or whoever — it passes among.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ ثُمَّ قَالَ
sentences.tr: thumma thumma qāla
sentences.l: Then — then he said,
sentences.n: The word 'then' is printed twice in a row in the edition; this looks like a compositor's repetition rather than deliberate emphasis, but it is kept here exactly as printed.

sentences.t: لَا تَشْرَبِ الرَّاحَ الَّا مِنْ يَدَيْ رَشًا * يَبْكِيكَ فِي رِقَّةِ الْمَعْنَى وَيُبْكِيهَا
sentences.tr: lā tashrabi al-rāḥa illā min yaday rashan * yabkīka fī riqqati al-maʿnā wa-yubkīhā
sentences.l: Drink not the wine except from the two hands of a young gazelle, who makes you weep in the tenderness of the meaning, and makes her weep.
sentences.i: Drink the wine from no hand but a gazelle-slim beauty's * whose tender meaning moves you both, together, to tears.
sentences.n: 'A young gazelle' (rashan) is the stock figure for a graceful beloved. The closing 'and makes her weep' plays on the wine itself seeming to weep as it is poured, alongside the two of them.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ بَعْدَ إِنْشَادِهِ قَبَّلَ أَيْدِيَهُمْ وَ شَرِبَ وَ سَكِرَ وَ تَمَايَلَ وَ أَنْشَدَ يَقُولُ شِعْرٌ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu baʿda inshādihi qabbala aydiyahum wa-shariba wa-sakira wa-tamāyala wa-anshada yaqūlu shiʿrun
sentences.l: Then, after his recitation, he kissed their hands, and drank, and became drunk, and swayed, and recited, saying, in verse:
sentences.i: Then, once he had finished, he kissed their hands, drank, grew drunk, swayed where he sat, and recited these lines:

sentences.t:
كُلُّ شَيءٍ مِنَ الدِّمَاءِ حَرَامٌ شُرْبُهُ * مَا خَلَا دَمَ الْعَنْقُودِ
فَاسْقِنِيهَا فِدًى لِعَيْنَيْكَ نَفْسِي * مِنْ غَزَالٍ وَطَارِفِي وَتَلِيدِي
sentences.tr:
kullu shayʾin mina al-dimāʾi ḥarāmun shurbuhu * mā khalā dama al-ʿanqūdi
fa-isqinīhā fidan li-ʿaynayki nafsī * min ghazālin wa-ṭārifī wa-talīdī
sentences.l:
Every kind of blood, its drinking is forbidden, except the blood of the grape-cluster.
So give it to me to drink — my soul be a ransom for your two eyes, O gazelle — [I give] my newly-gained and my inherited wealth.
sentences.i:
All blood is forbidden to drink * save the blood of the grape —
so pour it for me; my very soul I'd ransom for your eyes' sake, O gazelle * take all I own, the new and the old alike.
sentences.n: 'Blood of the grape-cluster' is a stock kenning for wine. 'My newly-gained and my inherited [wealth]' is a set pairing meaning 'all I own, new and old,' offered up for the beloved's sake.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ مَلَأَتِ الْقَدَحَ وَ نَاوَلَتْهَا لِأُخْتِهَا الْوُسْطَى فَأَخَذَتْهَا مِنْ يَدِهَا وَ شَكَرَتْهَا وَ شَرِبَتْ
sentences.tr: thumma malaʾati al-qadaḥa wa-nāwalathā li-ukhtihā al-wusṭā fa-akhadhathā min yadihā wa-shakarathā wa-sharibat
sentences.l: Then she filled the cup and handed it to her middle sister, and she took it from her hand, and thanked her, and drank.
sentences.i: Then she filled the cup and passed it to her middle sister, who took it from her hand, thanked her, and drank.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ مَلَأَتْ وَ نَاوَلَتْ لِصَاحِبَةِ السَّرِيرِ
sentences.tr: thumma malaʾat wa-nāwalat li-ṣāḥibati al-sarīri
sentences.l: Then she filled [a cup] and handed it to the mistress of the couch.
sentences.i: Then she filled a cup and gave it to the lady of the couch.
sentences.n: 'The mistress of the couch' seems to mean the sister who is mistress of the house, seated on the raised couch or divan.

sentences.t: وَ مَلَأَتْ كَأْسًا أُخْرَى وَ نَاوَلَتْهَا الْحَمَّالَ فَقَبَّلَ الْأَرْضَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهَا وَ شَكَرَ وَ شَرِبَ وَ أَنْشَدَ يَقُولُ شِعْرٌ
sentences.tr: wa-malaʾat kaʾsan ukhrā wa-nāwalathā al-ḥammāla fa-qabbala al-arḍa bayna yadayhā wa-shakara wa-shariba wa-anshada yaqūlu shiʿrun
sentences.l: And she filled another cup and handed it to the porter, and he kissed the ground before her, and thanked her, and drank, and recited, saying, in verse:
sentences.i: And she filled another cup and gave it to the porter, who kissed the ground before her, gave thanks, drank, and recited these lines:
sentences.n: Kissing the ground before someone is a gesture of extreme deference, offered here half in earnest and half in the play of the drinking game.

sentences.t:
هَاتِهَا بِاللهِ هَاتِ * مِنْ كُوْسٍ مُتْرَعَاتِ
وَاسْقِنِيْ مِنْهَا بِكَاسٍ * اِنَّهَا مَاءُ الْحَيَاةِ
sentences.tr:
hātihā bi-Allāhi hāti * min kūsin mutraʿātin
wa-isqinī minhā bi-kāsin * innahā māʾu al-ḥayāti
sentences.l:
Bring it, by God, bring [it], from cups brimful.
And give me to drink from it, with a cup — indeed it is the water of life.
sentences.i:
Bring it, by God, bring it, from cups filled to the brim —
and pour me a cup of it, for truly, it is the very water of life.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ تَقَدَّمَ إِلَى صَاحِبَةِ الْمَحَلِّ وَقَالَ يَا سِتِّي أَنَا عَبْدُكِ وَمَمْلُوكُكِ وَ خَدَّامُكِ وَأَنْشَدَ يَقُولُ
sentences.tr: thumma taqaddama ilā ṣāḥibati al-maḥalli wa-qāla yā sittī anā ʿabduki wa-mamlūkuki wa-khaddāmuki wa-anshada yaqūlu
sentences.l: Then he came forward to the mistress of the place and said, 'O my lady, I am your slave, and your bondsman, and your servant,' and recited, saying:
sentences.i: Then he stepped up to the lady of the house and said, 'O my lady, I am your slave, your bondsman, your servant,' and recited:
sentences.n: 'Sitti' (for classical 'sayyidatī', 'my lady') is a colloquial contraction, kept here as the edition prints it.

sentences.t:
عَلَى الْبَابِ عَبْدٌ مِنْ عَبِيدِكَ وَاقِفٌ * بِجُودِكَ وَالِاحْسَانِ مَا زَالَ مُعْتَرِفٌ
أَيَدْخُلُ يَا ذَاتَ الْمَحَاسِنِ كَيْ يَرَى * جَمَالَكِ إِنِّي وَالْهَوَى غَيْرُ مُنْصَرِفٌ
sentences.tr:
ʿalā al-bābi ʿabdun min ʿabīdiki wāqifun * bi-jūdiki wa-al-iḥsāni mā zāla muʿtarifun
a-yadkhulu yā dhāta al-maḥāsini kay yarā * jamālaki innī wa-al-hawā ghayru munṣarifun
sentences.l:
At the door stands a slave of your slaves, who has not ceased to confess your bounty and kindness.
May he enter, O possessor of graces, that he might see your beauty? Indeed I — and my passion — am not to be turned away.
sentences.i:
At your door stands one slave among your slaves * forever confessing your bounty and your kindness —
may he come in, O lady of many graces, to look * upon your beauty? For I, and my longing, will not be turned aside.
sentences.n: The archive points the possessive suffixes on 'your slaves' and 'your bounty' with the masculine ending even though the poem addresses a woman; kept as printed.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ طِبْ نَفْسًا وَاشْرَبْ هَنِيًا وَعَافِيَةً تَجْرِي مَجَارِيَ الصِّحَّةِ فَأَخَذَ الْكَأْسَ وَقَبَّلَ يَدَهَا وَتَرَنَّمَ وَأَنْشَدَ يَقُولُ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu ṭib nafsan wa-ishrab hanīan wa-ʿāfiyatan tajrī majāriya al-ṣiḥḥati fa-akhadha al-kaʾsa wa-qabbala yadahā wa-tarannama wa-anshada yaqūlu
sentences.l: So she said to him, 'Be at ease in yourself, and drink pleasantly, with wholesomeness running the courses of health.' And he took the cup, and kissed her hand, and hummed a tune, and recited, saying:
sentences.i: So she told him, 'Set your heart at ease, and drink in health and pleasure, wellness coursing through you.' He took the cup, kissed her hand, hummed a snatch of song, and recited:
sentences.n: 'Pleasantly' (hanīan) is printed here without the medial hamza that the same word carries a few lines earlier in verse ('hanīʾan') — a Middle Arabic simplification, vocalised as printed rather than corrected.

sentences.t:
نَاوَلَتْهَا شِبْهَ خَدَّيْهَا مُعَتَّقَةً * صِرْفاً كَانَ صِرْفاً كَانَ سَنَاهَا ضَوْءُ مِقْبَاسِ
فَقَبَّلْتُهَا وَقُلْتُ وَهِيَ ضَاحِكَةٌ * فَكَيْفَ تَسْقِي خُدُودَ النَّاسِ لِلنَّاسِ
قُلْتُ اشْرَبِي فَهِيَ مِنْ دَمْعِي وَحُمْرَتُهَا * دَمِي وَطَابَتْهَا فِي الْكَاسِ أَنْفَاسِي
sentences.tr:
nāwalathā shibha khaddayhā muʿattaqatan * ṣirfan kāna ṣirfan kāna sanāhā ḍawʾu miqbāsin
fa-qabbaltuhā wa-qultu wa-hiya ḍāḥikatun * fa-kayfa tasqī khudūda al-nāsi li-al-nāsi
qultu ishrabī fa-hiya min damʿī wa-ḥumratuhā * damī wa-ṭābathā fī al-kāsi anfāsī
sentences.l:
She handed me an aged wine in the likeness of her two cheeks, pure — pure — its radiance was the light of a lamp.
So I kissed it and said, while she laughed, 'How is it you give the cheeks of people to drink, to people?'
I said, 'Drink, for it is made of my tears, and its redness is my blood, and its sweetness in the cup is my breath.'
sentences.i:
She handed me a vintage the likeness of her own two cheeks * pure, purely pure, its glow the glow of a lit lamp.
I kissed it, and said, as she laughed, * 'How is it you pour out people's very cheeks for people to drink?'
I said, 'Then drink — for it is made of my tears, its redness * my blood, and its sweetness in the cup, my breath.'
sentences.n: The cupbearer's flushed cheeks are likened to the wine's own colour; the wine is imagined as a distillation of her beauty, so that giving it to drink is 'giving people's cheeks to people.'

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ مُجِيبَةً عَلَيْهِ شِعْرٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat mujībatan ʿalayhi shiʿrun
sentences.l: Then she said, answering him, in verse:
sentences.i: Then she answered him with these lines:

sentences.t: إِنْ كُنْتَ يَا صَاحِ مِنْ أَجْلِي بَكَيْتَ دَمًا * هَاتِ اسْتَعِينِيهَا عَلَى الْعَيْنَيْنِ وَالرَّاسِ
sentences.tr: in kunta yā ṣāḥi min ajlī bakayta daman * hāti istaʿīnīhā ʿalā al-ʿaynayni wa-al-rāsi
sentences.l: If you, O friend, wept blood on my account, then bring it — help yourself with it against the eyes and the head.
sentences.i: If, my friend, you have wept blood for my sake * then bring it — let it be your remedy, for eyes and head alike.
sentences.n: Both imperatives ('bring' and 'help yourself') are pointed as feminine in the print, which sits oddly with 'O friend' (masculine); the line may be shifting address to a cupbearer mid-verse, or the text may be corrupt. Kept exactly as printed.

sentences.t: قَالَ فَأَخَذَتِ الصَّبِيَّةُ الْقَدَحَ وَشَرِبَتْهُ وَنَزَلَتْ عِنْدَ أُخْتِهَا
sentences.tr: qāla fa-akhadhati al-ṣabiyyatu al-qadaḥa wa-sharibathu wa-nazalat ʿinda ukhtihā
sentences.l: He said: So the girl took the cup and drank it, and settled down beside her sister.
sentences.i: He said: So the girl took the cup, drained it, and settled back beside her sister.

sentences.t: وَمَا زَالُوا يَشْرَبُونَ وَالْحَمَّالُ فِي وَسَطِهِمْ وَهُمْ فِي رَقْصٍ وَضَحِكٍ وَغِنَاءٍ وَأَشْعَارٍ وَمُوَشَّحَاتٍ
sentences.tr: wa-mā zālū yashrabūna wa-al-ḥammālu fī wasaṭihim wa-hum fī raqṣin wa-ḍaḥikin wa-ghināʾin wa-ashʿārin wa-muwashshaḥātin
sentences.l: And they did not cease drinking, with the porter in their midst, they being amid dancing, and laughing, and singing, and poems, and strophic songs.
sentences.i: And on they drank, the porter in their midst, amid dancing and laughter, song, verse, and strophic songs.
sentences.n: 'Muwashshaḥāt' are strophic, multi-rhymed songs, a lighter musical form distinct from the classical monorhymed verses quoted elsewhere in this scene.

sentences.t: وَصَارَ الْحَمَّالُ مَعَهُمْ فِي هِرَاشٍ وَبَوْسٍ وَعَضٍّ وَفَرْكٍ وَ جَسٍّ وَلَمْسٍ وَخِرَاعٍ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣāra al-ḥammālu maʿahum fī hirāshin wa-bawsin wa-ʿaḍḍin wa-farkin wa-jassin wa-lamsin wa-khirāʿin
sentences.l: And the porter fell, with them, into scuffling, and kissing, and biting, and rubbing, and groping, and touching, and wanton play.
sentences.i: And the porter fell in with them — roughhousing, kissing, biting, rubbing, groping, touching, romping wantonly, all together.
sentences.n: The last word, 'khirāʿ', is printed as given and its exact sense is uncertain; it most likely stands for 'khalāʿa' (wanton dissoluteness), which is how it is rendered here, though the edition's spelling is kept unaltered.

sentences.t: وَهَذِهِ تُلَقِّمُهُ وَهَذِهِ تَلْكُمُهُ وَهَذِهِ تَلْطِمُهُ وَهَذِهِ بِالْمَشْمُومِ يَخْدُمُهُ
sentences.tr: wa-hādhihi tulaqqimuhu wa-hādhihi talkumuhu wa-hādhihi talṭimuhu wa-hādhihi bi-al-mashmūmi yakhdumuhu
sentences.l: And this one feeds him morsels, and this one strikes him with her fist, and this one slaps him, and this one serves him with sweet-smelling herbs.
sentences.i: This one would pop tidbits into his mouth, this one would cuff him, this one would slap him, and this one would ply him with sweet basil.
sentences.n: 'Al-mashmūm' ('the thing smelled') denotes fragrant herbs such as sweet basil, traditionally passed around at Nights drinking parties for their scent.

sentences.t: وَهُوَ مَعَهُمْ فِي أَلَذِّ عَيْشٍ كَأَنَّهُ قَاعِدٌ فِي الْجَنَّةِ بَيْنَ حُورِ الْعَيْنِ
sentences.tr: wa-huwa maʿahum fī aladhdhi ʿayshin ka-annahu qāʿidun fī al-jannati bayna ḥūri al-ʿayni
sentences.l: And he was with them in the most delightful of lives, as though he were sitting in Paradise among the wide-eyed houris.
sentences.i: And there he sat among them in the sweetest life imaginable, as if he were seated in Paradise among the dark-eyed houris.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَزَالُوا كَذَلِكَ حَتَّى لَعِبَتِ الْخَمْرَةُ فِي رُوسِهِمْ وَ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yazālū ka-dhālika ḥattā laʿibati al-khamratu fī rūsihim wa-
sentences.l: And they did not cease thus until the wine played in their heads, and —
sentences.i: And so it went on, until the wine had climbed into their heads, and —
sentences.n: 'Their heads' (rūsihim) is printed without the hamza that 'ruʾūs' properly carries — the same kind of dropped-hamza spelling seen above in 'hanīan' — and is vocalised here as printed, read the way the colloquial pronunciation actually drops it.

sentences.t: عَنَّوْلَهُمْ فَلَمَّا تَحَكَّمَ الشَّرَابُ مَعَهُمْ قَامَتِ الْبَوَّابَةُ وَ تَجَرَّدَتْ مِنْ ثِيَابِهَا وَصَارَتْ عُرْيَانَةً وَ أَرْخَتْ شَعْرَهَا عَلَيْهَا سِتْرًا وَ أَرْمَتْ نَفْسَهَا فِي الْبُحَيْرَةِ
sentences.tr: ʿannawlahum fa-lammā taḥakkama al-sharābu maʿahum qāmati al-bawwābatu wa-tajarradat min thiyābihā wa-ṣārat ʿuryānatan wa-arkhat shaʿrahā ʿalayhā sitran wa-armat nafsahā fī al-buḥayrati
sentences.l: It occurred to them — and when the wine had gained mastery over them, the doorkeeper rose up and stripped off her clothes, and became naked, and let down her hair over herself as a covering, and cast herself into the pool.
sentences.i: A notion had taken them; and when the wine had mastered them, the doorkeeper rose and stripped off her clothes and stood naked, letting down her hair over herself for a covering, and threw herself into the pool.
sentences.n: The archive prints the opening as one unspaced word, عنولهم. It most plausibly represents عَنَّ لَهُمْ, 'it occurred to them,' the tail of a sentence begun before this passage, but the exact word division cannot be recovered with confidence and is kept exactly as printed.

sentences.t: وَ لَعِبَتْ فِي الْمَاءِ وَبَطْبَطَتْ وَتَغَلَّتْ وَأَخَذَتِ الْمَاءَ فِي فَمِهَا وَ مَجَّتْ عَلَى الْحَمَّالِ
sentences.tr: wa-laʿibat fī al-māʾi wa-baṭbaṭat wa-taghallat wa-akhadhati al-māʾa fī famihā wa-majjat ʿalā al-ḥammāli
sentences.l: and she played in the water, and splashed about, and made it seethe, and took the water into her mouth, and spat it out over the porter.
sentences.i: She played in the water, splashing and churning it up, then took a mouthful and spat it out over the porter.
sentences.n: بَطْبَطَتْ and تَغَلَّتْ are colloquial, sound-suggestive verbs for boisterous splashing in water; their exact nuance cannot be fixed precisely, but the sense of playful commotion is clear.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ غَسَلَتْ أَعْضَاهَا وَ بَيْنَ أَفْخَاذِهَا ثُمَّ طَلَعَتْ مِنَ الْمَاءِ وَ رَمَتْ رُوحَهَا فِي حِجْرِ الْحَمَّالِ
sentences.tr: thumma ghasalat aʿḍāhā wa-bayna afkhādhihā thumma ṭalaʿat mina al-māʾi wa-ramat rūḥahā fī ḥijri al-ḥammāli
sentences.l: Then she washed her members and between her thighs, then came up out of the water and threw her very self into the porter's lap.
sentences.i: Then she washed her limbs and between her thighs, then rose up out of the water and flung herself straight into the porter's lap.

sentences.t: وَ قَالَتْ لَهُ يَا سَيِّدِي يَا حَبِيبِي أَيْشْ اسْمُ هَذَا وَ أَشَارَتْ إِلَى فَرْجِهَا
sentences.tr: wa-qālat lahu yā sayyidī yā ḥabībī aysh ismu hādhā wa-ashārat ilā farjihā
sentences.l: and said to him, "O my master, O my beloved, what is the name of this?" — and she pointed to her vulva.
sentences.i: and said to him, "My lord, my darling, what do you call this?" — pointing to her vulva.
sentences.n: أَيْشْ, "what," is a colloquial contraction of أَيُّ شَيْءٍ, "which thing," recurring through this dialogue.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْحَمَّالُ رَحِمَكِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-ḥammālu raḥimaki
sentences.l: The porter said, "Your womb."
sentences.i: The porter said, "Your womb."

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ إِيهِ أَمَا تَسْتَحِي
sentences.tr: fa-qālat īhi amā tastaḥī
sentences.l: She said, "Hah! Have you no shame?"
sentences.i: "Hah!" she said. "Have you no shame?"

sentences.t: وَ مَسَكَتْهُ مِنْ رَقَبَتِهِ وَ صَارَتْ تَصُكُّهُ
sentences.tr: wa-masakathu min raqabatihi wa-ṣārat taṣukkuhu
sentences.l: and she seized him by his neck, and fell to striking him.
sentences.i: and she took hold of him by the neck and set about cuffing him.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ فَرْجُكِ فَسَكَّتَهُ ثَانِيًا عَلَى قَفَاهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla farjuki fa-sakkatahu thāniyan ʿalā qafāhu
sentences.l: He said, "Your vulva." So she struck him quiet a second time on the back of his neck.
sentences.i: He said, "Your vulva," so she cuffed him a second time on the back of the neck.
sentences.n: Printed سكته, with a single ت, is grammatically masculine ("he silenced him"), though the subject is the woman; a doubled ت (the expected feminine سكّتته) appears to have been lost in printing, and the same happens again below. The edition also alternates between the roots صكّ and سكّ/سكّت for "to strike, cuff" throughout this passage; both are rendered here as "struck, cuffed."

sentences.t: وَ قَالَتْ وَا إِي وَا قَبِيحُ مَا تَسْتَحِي
sentences.tr: wa-qālat wā ī wā qabīḥu mā tastaḥī
sentences.l: and she said, "Oh! Ay! Oh, shameless one, have you no shame?"
sentences.i: and she cried, "Fie, fie! For shame — have you no shame at all?"

sentences.t: فَقَالَ كُسُّكِ فَقَالَتْ إِيهِ أَنْتَ مَا تَسْتَحِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla kussuki fa-qālat īhi anta mā tastaḥī
sentences.l: He said, "Your cunt." She said, "Hah! You have no shame?"
sentences.i: He said, "Your cunt." "Hah!" she said. "Have you no shame at all?"

sentences.t: عَلَى عِرْضِكَ ثُمَّ لَكَمَتْهُ بِيَدِهَا وَ ضَرَبَتْهُ
sentences.tr: ʿalā ʿirḍika thumma lakamathu bi-yadihā wa-ḍarabathu
sentences.l: — on your honor?" Then she punched him with her hand and struck him.
sentences.i: — on your honor?" Then she punched him with her fist and struck him.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْحَمَّالُ زُنْبُورُكِ فَنَزَلَتْ عَلَيْهِ الْكُبْرَى بِالضَّرْبِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-ḥammālu zunbūruki fa-nazalat ʿalayhi al-kubrā bi-al-ḍarbi
sentences.l: The porter said, "Your hornet," and the eldest came down on him with blows.
sentences.i: The porter said, "Your hornet," and the eldest of them came down on him with blows.

sentences.t: وَ قَالَتْ لَهُ لَا تَقُلْ كَذَا
sentences.tr: wa-qālat lahu lā taqul kadhā
sentences.l: and said to him, "Do not say that!"
sentences.i: and told him, "Don't say that!"

sentences.t: فَصَارَ الْحَمَّالُ كُلَّمَا قَالَ بِاسْمٍ زَادُوهُ ضَرْبًا
sentences.tr: fa-ṣāra al-ḥammālu kullamā qāla bi-ismin zādūhu ḍarban
sentences.l: and so it was that every time the porter spoke a name, they gave him more blows,
sentences.i: and so it went: every time the porter offered a name, they only beat him more,

sentences.t: وَ لَمْ يَكُنْ إِلَّا أَنْ ذَابَ قَفَاهُ مِنَ الصَّكِّ وَ جَعَلُوهُ أُضْحُوكَةً بَيْنَهُمْ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yakun illā an dhāba qafāhu mina al-ṣakki wa-jaʿalūhu uḍḥūkatan baynahum
sentences.l: and it was no time at all before the back of his neck had melted away from the striking, and they made him a laughingstock among themselves,
sentences.i: until, in no time, the back of his neck was worn raw from the blows, and they made him their standing joke,

sentences.t: إِلَى أَنْ قَالَ وَ مَا اسْمُهُ عِنْدَكُنَّ
sentences.tr: ilā an qāla wa-mā ismuhu ʿindakunna
sentences.l: until he said, "And what is its name, with you?"
sentences.i: until at last he asked, "Well then, what do you call it?"

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ حَبَقُ الْجُسُورِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat ḥabaqu al-jusūri
sentences.l: So she said, "Basil of the Canals."
sentences.i: "Basil of the Canals," she said.
sentences.n: حَبَقُ الْجُسُورِ, "basil of the canals/dykes," is the fanciful, decorous name she wants used for her genitals, in place of the porter's blunt anatomical guesses.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْحَمَّالُ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ عَلَى السَّلَامَةِ طَيِّبٌ يَا حَبَقَ الْجُسُورِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-ḥammālu al-ḥamdu lillāhi ʿalā al-salāmati ṭayyibun yā ḥabaqa al-jusūri
sentences.l: The porter said, "Praise be to God for safety! Very well, O Basil of the Canals."
sentences.i: The porter said, "Thank God that's over! Very well then, O Basil of the Canals."

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُمْ دَوَّرُوا الْكَأْسَ وَ الطَّاسَ
sentences.tr: thumma innahum dawwarū al-kaʾsa wa-al-ṭāsa
sentences.l: Then they passed the cup and the bowl around.
sentences.i: Then they passed the cup and the bowl round again.

sentences.t: وَ قَامَتِ الثَّانِيَةُ وَ خَلَعَتْ ثِيَابَهَا وَ رَمَتْ نَفْسَهَا فِي حِجْرِ الْحَمَّالِ وَ أَوْمَتْ إِلَى حِرِّهَا
sentences.tr: wa-qāmati al-thāniyatu wa-khalaʿat thiyābahā wa-ramat nafsahā fī ḥijri al-ḥammāli wa-awmat ilā ḥirrihā
sentences.l: And the second one rose up, and took off her clothes, and threw herself into the porter's lap, and gestured toward her cunt,
sentences.i: Then the second of them rose, stripped off her clothes, threw herself into the porter's lap, and gestured toward her cunt,
sentences.n: حِرّ is the plain anatomical term for the vulva, distinct from the more decorous فَرْج used elsewhere in this passage.
